title: A source whose markup a browser has to repair
why: SH569's archetype fails at the FETCH layer; this is a 200 whose body is wrong, and the two are separate because a scanner cannot report what a fetch already refused. Nothing else in the corpus is malformed — every page was typed by somebody who closed their tags, so `tokenize`, `scanPage` and `stripNonMarkup` had only ever been measured against markup a browser would not have had to repair, and a real source is repaired constantly and silently. Six traits, one per known cost: an unclosed div and section so a block's extent is a guess; no <title> at all, which Page requires; a 265-character title, which is SH544 as a fixture rather than as a story; a nested form the parser must not read as two; a <base href> that disagrees with the serving path, so every relative reference has two resolutions and only one is the browser's; and a declared charset the bytes contradict, which is where mojibake enters as CONTENT rather than as a terminal artefact. That last one is judged on the bytes and never on what a terminal prints — the checklist records getting it wrong from the other direction.

notes.means: the crawl states that it resolved relative URLs against the page and not against the declared base, so the one resolution a browser would not have chosen is reported rather than silently recorded
